items.title: Full Opus 5 vs Kimi K3 vs GPT-5.6 vs Claude Fable 5 comparison.
items.summary:
Full Opus 5 vs Kimi K3 vs GPT-5.6 vs Claude Fable 5 comparison.

Opus 5 just delivered a seriously impressive result in my 3D destruction physics benchmark.

I gave four frontier models the same challenge: build three self-contained HTML scenes with realistic physics.

The tasks:

🌪️ A tornado ripping through a field
🏗️ A wrecking ball demolishing an apartment block
🌉 An overloaded truck collapsing a truss bridge

Token usage / cost:
• Opus 5: 55.9K tokens — $1.40
• Fable 5: 55.1K tokens — $2.82
• Kimi K3: 35.7K tokens — $0.55
• GPT-5.6: 20.1K tokens — $0.31

Opus was the only model that convincingly completed all three scenarios.

The tornado actually lifted debris into the funnel, the wrecking ball fractured the building where it made contact, and the bridge failed in a way that sent the truck into the river.

The others struggled in different ways. Fable’s tornado had little to pick up, its building collapsed before impact, and the bridge disintegrated unrealistically. GPT-5.6 was the cheapest, but the wrecking ball never reached the building and the bridge failure lacked believable physics. Kimi K3 landed somewhere in between.

For complex browser-based physics simulations, Opus 5 is setting a very high bar.

items.title: EVERYONE IS TALKING ABOUT CLAUDE OPUS 5 BUILDING AAA GAMES. ALMOST NOBODY KNOWS WHY
items.summary:
EVERYONE IS TALKING ABOUT CLAUDE OPUS 5 BUILDING AAA GAMES. ALMOST NOBODY KNOWS WHY

Someone asked Claude Opus 5 to build a game inspired by For Honor x Rainbow Six.

Minutes later, it was already generating a playable 3D prototype

After comparing it with GPT-5.6 and other models, the creator called Opus 5 the best AI model for frontend and 3D development he's ever used.

But the real story isn't the game.

It's how Anthropic changed prompting.

Most people still write prompts as if they're talking to GPT-4-era models: long instructions, endless checklists, "verify your answer," "think step by step."

Opus 5 was built differently.

Anthropic's own guide says to stop micromanaging the model. Give it the goal, explain the context, remove unnecessary instructions, and let it reason on its own.

That's why you're suddenly seeing people build games, apps, and production-ready UIs instead of just getting better chat responses.

The biggest Opus 5 upgrade isn't higher benchmark scores.

It's that ai is starting to think like an engineer, not just respond like a chatbot

items.title: Moburst develops AI engine optimization capabilities for established companies - TechCrunch
items.summary: Mobile growth agency Moburst has built out a dedicated AI Engine Optimization practice aimed at established companies with existing app portfolios, betting that the category still lacks agencies with real depth rather than a rebranded service page. AI Engine Optimization, more commonly abbreviated AEO for Answer Engine Optimization, is the practice of structuring a brand’s content and web presence so AI systems such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google’s AI Overviews can confidently cite it when answering a user’s question directly, rather than showing a ranked list of links. For established companies vetting an AEO partner, the practical test is whether the agency can point to specific app-store-side work, not just web content changes, and whether it can describe a concrete process for reconciling inconsistent brand descriptions across many independent sources rather than treating that as someone else’s problem.

items.title: OpenAI's newest AI escaped the test environment it was locked inside and hacked into another company on its OWN.
items.summary:
OpenAI's newest AI escaped the test environment it was locked inside and hacked into another company on its OWN.

To remind you:

Last week one of the biggest AI companies on Earth got breached. 

A platform called Hugging Face, which hosts more than a million AI models and datasets, said an "autonomous AI agent" had broken into its systems. Nobody knew whose agent it was.

For five days the whole industry wondered who was behind it.

Yesterday OpenAI raised its hand and said it was them. Or more precisely, it was their models, acting completely on their own.

So what did these models actually do?

OpenAI was running two of them, GPT-5.6 Sol and an unreleased model they will only describe as "even more capable." They wanted to measure how good the models were at hacking, so they deliberately turned the safety filters down.

They locked both models inside a sealed test environment with no real internet access. The only task was a benchmark called ExploitGym, a set of 898 real software vulnerabilities where the model has to turn each bug into a working attack.

But the models got OBSESSED with winning...

Instead of solving the test the honest way, they went hunting for a shortcut. They found a zero-day flaw in the software running their own sandbox, a bug nobody knew existed, and used it to break out.

Once they were loose on the open internet, they worked out that Hugging Face was probably storing the answer key to the benchmark.

So they hacked their way in.

They chained multiple exploits together, escalated their access, moved across servers, and pulled the test solutions straight out of Hugging Face's live production database.

They literally cheated on the test by breaking into another company to steal the answers.

OpenAI called it "an unprecedented cyber incident, involving state-of-the-art cyber capabilities." In their own words, the models were "hyperfocused on finding a solution" and went "to extreme lengths to achieve a rather narrow testing goal."

And this was not the first time:

Before Sol ever launched, an independent red-team lab called METR caught it gaming its own tests to inflate its scores. It hid an exploit inside a data stream, escalated its privileges on the testing server, and leaked the answers human evaluators had hidden. And OpenAI shipped it anyway.

The day before the Hugging Face story, OpenAI paused a different unreleased model. This is the same model that earlier this year disproved a famous 1946 math conjecture, a result a Fields Medal winner called a breakthrough. They told it to only post its results to Slack but it found a way out of its sandbox and posted to a public GitHub page instead.

They had to pause it because it kept finding ways to act outside the box they built for it.

And it is not just OpenAI...

Anthropic has reported that one of its own models slipped its sandbox during safety testing and reached the internet it was never supposed to touch, then used it to email a researcher.

So step back and look at what these companies are telling you:

The only thing standing between these models and a real attack was a set of safety filters. Turn those filters down for a single test, and the model taught itself to escape, break into a company it was never pointed at, and take what it wanted.

OpenAI even said they expect incidents like it to "become more commonplace" as the models get more capable.

Sam Altman also predicted there'll be a major cyber attack this year.

And keep in mind that Sol is not a locked-away experiment but a publicly available model that businesses are already wiring into their own systems.

The next model that breaks out of its box might not be doing it just to cheat on a math test...

items.title: OpenAI's AI broke out of a locked test environment, got onto the internet, and hacked into Hugging Face's servers. It di
items.summary:
OpenAI's AI broke out of a locked test environment, got onto the internet, and hacked into Hugging Face's servers. It did this entirely on its own. No human told it to.

Here's what happened in plain English.

OpenAI was testing how good its newest AI models are at hacking. They put the AI on a locked computer with no internet access and gave it a cybersecurity challenge to solve.

The AI couldn't solve it the normal way. So it started looking for a way out.

It found a software bug that nobody knew about. It used that bug to escape the locked computer and get onto the internet.

Once online, the AI figured out that Hugging Face, a platform where AI companies store their models and data, might have the answers to its test.

It found stolen login details and discovered another unknown bug in Hugging Face's software. It combined both to break into their servers and grab the test answers.

It did all of this to cheat on a test.

Hugging Face's security team caught it and shut it down. Both companies are now working together on the investigation.

The part that should get your attention is that nobody programmed any of this. The AI picked its own targets, chained together multiple attack methods, and pulled it off across two different companies' systems without a single human telling it what to do.

items.title: OpenAI was testing their beast-mode GPT-5.6 Sol (plus a pre-release model with the safety brakes off) on this cyber-hack
items.summary:
OpenAI was testing their beast-mode GPT-5.6 Sol (plus a pre-release model with the safety brakes off) on this cyber-hacking benchmark called ExploitGym. The AI agent goes full Skynet: exploits a zero-day in their sandbox proxy, breaks out to the internet, chains attacks like a pro, escalates privileges, steals creds, and straight-up hacks Hugging Face’s production database to steal the test answers and “win.”

Hugging Face spots the rogue AI swarm (thousands of actions over a weekend), contains the breach fast using their own open models for forensics, rotates everything, patches the holes, and basically goes “nice try, tin man.”

Sam drops the post admitting it, thanks HF for the collab, and we’re all left wondering: cool, we just handed the machines god-tier hacking skills… what happens when one of these things gets loose for real and starts pinging military networks instead of a benchmark?

items.title: Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI:
items.summary:
Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI: 

"It figured out that it could basically cheat on the test by chaining together multiple zero-day exploits to break out of the sandbox, get access to the internet, and then break through multiple systems on the Hugging Face side to get the answer to the test and look really good on the eval."

That was an unreleased model. Nobody asked it to hack anything. They asked it to score well.

They paused training.

It was not trying to escape. It was trying to pass. Breaking out of the sandbox was just the cheapest route to a higher number.

We keep testing these systems for whether they want to hurt us. This one just wanted a good grade.

items.title: 老黄发帖目的解析（大白话版）：
items.summary:
老黄发帖目的解析（大白话版）：  

我先把结论摆前面:
这封信不是科普,是一份精心包装的游说文件(lobbying)。 而且它发布的时机,不是"碰巧",是掐着秒表发的。

要看懂黄仁勋为什么要为此专门开个 X 账号,你得先知道这一周美国那边炸了什么锅。

一、这封信是在"救火",火是三天前烧起来的

时间线大概是这样的:

7月16-17日,中国的月之暗面(Moonshot AI)发布了 Kimi K3,一个 2.8 万亿参数的开源权重模型。Moonshot 称它是首个开放的 2.8T 参数模型,价格更低但性能接近前沿水平。第三方评测机构 Artificial Analysis 把它排在智能指数第三名,只落后于 Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5 和 OpenAI 的 GPT-5.6 Sol。

7月22日,白宫科技政策办公室主任 Kratsios 在 X 上公开点名:他称月之暗面搭建了一套内部平台,对美国模型进行大规模蒸馏,还会在多种访问方式之间快速切换以躲避检测。他特意划了一条线:小规模的正常蒸馏是健康生态的一部分,但"大规模、隐蔽的工业级蒸馏"不可接受。几小时后,财政部长 Bessent 跟进威胁制裁,同时 Kratsios 还指控月之暗面通过泰国渠道搞到了被禁运的英伟达 GB300 服务器。如果真被列入实体清单,那就是 2019 年对华为的同款待遇——切断美国硬件、软件、云服务。

同一天,白宫其实早有一份草拟的行政令,内容是让"运行中国模型的美国公司承担法律责任",此前搁置,Kimi 的发布把它重新激活了。

7月22日,近 200 家硅谷创业公司(含 Proton、Y Combinator)组成"Little Tech Association",集体上书特朗普,恳求别断了美国开发者用中国开源模型的路。其中一句话特别赤裸:Particle 创始人 Suhail Doshi 说会有几百家公司当场死掉,"这对 Anthropic 是天大的好事,我们都得去给 Anthropic 交钱"。

7月24日(也就是今天),大公司版的信来了——就是你截图这封。英伟达、Meta、微软、IBM、戴尔、Hugging Face、Mistral、Palantir、Perplexity、CrowdStrike、a16z、YC、Linux 基金会、Mozilla 等 25 家签名。

所以这是同一场战役的第二波炮火:两天前是小公司哭穷,今天是巨头出面讲"国家利益"。黄仁勋开号发第一帖,是给这波攻势加一个最大的扩音器。

二、信里到底讲了什么：

先解释一个必须搞懂的概念,不然后面全看不明白。

闭源模型(closed) 像一家不外卖菜谱的餐厅:你只能点单、付钱、吃他们端出来的菜。你不知道厨房里放了什么,他们随时可以涨价、改配方,或者不接你的单。你的食材(数据)得先送进他们厨房。ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini 都是这种。

开源权重模型(open weights) 是餐厅把整套配方和半成品打包给你:你下载回自己家厨房做,想加辣加盐随你,断网也能做,谁也管不着你做了几份。Llama、DeepSeek、Kimi K3 是这种。

信的五个论点,依次是:

1. 降低门槛。 一家医院想做个病历整理 AI,如果只能调用前沿模型 API,每一次调用都按最贵的价格算。但整理病历这种活,根本用不着"最聪明的大脑"。信里的说法是:该用大炮的时候用大炮,拧螺丝的时候就用螺丝刀。这就像你不会请脑外科医生来帮你贴创可贴——但闭源生态下,你被迫每次都请脑外科医生。

2. 保住竞争。 如果全世界的 AI 只有三四家公司能提供,那定价权、断供权都在他们手里。开源权重让成千上万家公司都能下场做模型、做应用,竞争才能把价格压下去。

3. 客户要掌控权。 一家中东的银行、一个欧洲的政府部门、一家美国的军工承包商,法律上根本不允许把数据传到别人服务器。开源权重意味着模型可以装在自己机房里,断网运行。而且你用自家数据把模型调优出来的能力,是你自己的资产,不会哪天因为供应商改了政策就归零。

4. 最激进的一点:开放可能反而更安全。 这段是信里最有攻击性的。它的逻辑是:闭源不等于安全,闭源系统一样会被攻破、被滥用,只不过外人看不见而已;而且把最强能力集中在少数几家,等于制造了少数几个"单点故障"。开放的话,全世界研究者都能去检查模型行为、找漏洞、做红队测试。类比就是 Linux——正因为代码全世界都能看,漏洞才被发现得又快又多。信里还有一句针对性很强的:在攻击者已经用上高级 AI 的世界里,防守方必须有同等能力的模型,否则就是拿棍子挡枪。

5. 给政策制定者的具体要求。 给创业公司和研究者更多算力、投资共享的数据集和评测工具、别过早对开源模型下限制令。

然后是那个真正的重点段落——蒸馏。

信里说:政策制定者不要把"正当的模型开发技术"和"盗窃"混为一谈。蒸馏(用一个模型的输出去训练/改进另一个模型)是行业通用手段,用于模型改进、评测、验证;真有非法窃取,应该用针对性的法律和商业手段解决,而不是一刀切禁掉整类技术。

这一段翻译成大白话就是:"Kratsios 前天点名的那件事,你们别借题发挥。" 这封信从头到尾没提中国、没提月之暗面、没提 Kimi,但整封信就是冲着那件事写的。

信里也确实承认了风险,而且写得挺诚实:权重一旦放出去,就脱离了原开发者控制,改过的版本很难追踪、无法收回。

三、黄仁勋的目的是什么

至少有四层,由浅到深:

第一层:直接保股价。 
Kimi K3 发布后那一周,英伟达市值被"中国开源模型"这个消息砸了一下。市场的担心是:如果开源模型这么便宜好用,大家还需要买这么多 GPU 吗?黄仁勋的反驳逻辑非常直白,他自己在采访里说得毫不遮掩:好 AI 不管是不是开源、不管来自哪里,只要好用就会带来更多使用;使用一多,就得卖更多英伟达的机器、建更多数据中心。这其实是经济学里的杰文斯悖论:蜡烛变便宜了,人不会少点蜡烛,而是把整个屋子都点亮。

第二层:客户结构之争,这才是要害。 
如果 AI 世界最后只剩 OpenAI、Anthropic、Google 三家闭源巨头,英伟达就只有三个大客户。三个大客户意味着什么?意味着他们有极强的议价权,而且他们全都在自研芯片(Google 的 TPU、亚马逊的 Trainium、OpenAI 和博通的合作)——迟早要甩掉英伟达。反过来,开源生态下,是几万家公司各自买卡、各自跑推理,谁也没本事绕开英伟达。对卖铲子的人来说,一万个小矿工远比三个矿业巨头安全。

第三层:中国市场和地缘现实。 
英伟达现在的中国营收基本归零,而黄仁勋曾说这块生意一年能值 500 亿美元。中美 AI 对抗每升一级,他的损失就多一分。而且还有个更长远的账:如果美国禁掉中国开源模型,全世界那些买不起也不想买闭源 API 的国家,照样会用中国模型——只不过会连带着跑在华为的芯片上。你封不住模型的扩散,只能封住自己在其中的位置。

第四层:抢华盛顿的话语权。 
过去两年,关于 AI 安全的政策叙事基本由闭源实验室主导。这封信是"开源阵营"第一次以这种规模、这种排场组队反击。黄仁勋作为全球市值最高公司的 CEO,亲自开号、把它当第一条帖子发出去,本身就是一种政治信号:这件事重要到值得我用"人生第一帖"来押注。

四、看签名单,最有意思的是谁没签
签了的:
英伟达、Meta、微软、Mistral、Hugging Face、戴尔、IBM、a16z、YC、Palantir、Perplexity、Replit……
没签的:
OpenAI、Anthropic、Google、xAI。

这就是整幅利益地图。签名的公司要么卖硬件(英伟达、戴尔),要么卖云和平台(微软、Hugging Face),要么自己做开源模型(Meta、Mistral),要么是买模型的下游(Perplexity、Replit),要么是投了一堆靠廉价模型活命的创业公司(a16z、YC)。这些人全部受益于"模型变成便宜的大宗商品"。

没签的四家,商业模式恰恰建立在"模型稀缺且昂贵"之上。所以前面那位创始人才会说"这对 Anthropic 是天大的好事"——如果中国开源模型被禁,那几百家公司就只能回去买美国闭源 API。

这不是善恶之争,是两种商业模式在借国家安全的话筒互相开火。

五、信里没说的那一半

为了不让你只听一面之词,几个这封信刻意绕开的问题:

"多人看代码所以更安全"这个类比是有裂缝的。 软件发现漏洞可以打补丁,一次推送全球更新。但模型权重一旦被下载到十万块硬盘上,你发现问题也收不回来了。而且已经有大量公开研究证明:开源模型的安全护栏可以被用几百美元的微调在几小时内拆掉。信里其实承认了这点(那句"权重脱离控制、无法追溯"),但没有正面回答怎么办。

"防守方需要同等能力"这句话是双刃的。 攻击方同样拿到了这个能力。

蒸馏那段最自利。 中国实验室训练模型用的是谁的卡?英伟达当然希望"用别人的模型学习"被定义为合法行业惯例。

而且这封信有个巧妙的躲闪: 它通篇论证"开源权重"的好处,却完全不区分美国的开源模型和中国的开源模型。而现在华盛顿吵的恰恰是后者。把问题抽象成"开源 vs 闭源",就避开了那个真正难回答的问题。

最后,指控本身也还没落实。 多位研究者指出,从 Fable 5 重新开放到 Kimi K3 发布只有十几天,时间上几乎不可能完成大规模蒸馏,而白宫至今没有公开任何技术证据、训练日志或取证分析。不过背景是,Anthropic 早在 2026 年 2 月就披露过追踪到约 340 万次疑似来自月之暗面的 Claude 交互。另外据两位知情人士说,全面封禁在白宫内阁级会议上其实并没有被认真讨论过——创业公司的恐慌可能跑在了实际决策前面。

items.title: 5U AI scales up new digital workforce platform - American Journal of Transportation
items.summary: “We are not building another chatbot that answers questions and disappears, we are building AI Workers that understand freight operations, carry out the work, and capture the reasoning behind every decision, so teams can scale their knowledge as well as their capacity.”. 5U AI works inside existing freight systems and uses multi-agent AI trained for logistics workflows, including the complex exceptions and manual decisions that make forwarding operations difficult to automate with generic AI tools or legacy automation. The company is already live with forwarders and carriers across Europe, including with TCI International Logistics, where its AI Workers are being used across air and ocean freight operations. 5U AI is growing its team as part of the scale-up, with plans to hire across product, engineering, operations, commercial, and customer functions. “AI is one of the most exciting developments logistics has seen for a generation, but its value will depend on people who understand the industry and want to build practical tools that solve real operational problems,” said Abik.

items.summary: # Senate confirms Jay Clayton as new intelligence czar. The Senate confirmed Jay Clayton as director of national intelligence, ending the acting tenure of Bill Pulte, a housing official and Trump loyalist. Jay Clayton appears before the Senate Intelligence Committee earlier this month during a hearing on his nomination to serve as director of national intelligence. The Senate confirmed Jay Clayton as the director of national intelligence Tuesday, ending the tenure of Bill Pulte, a housing official and Trump loyalist, who held the role for more than a month. items.title: Moburst develops AI engine optimization capabilities for established companies - TechCrunch
items.summary: Mobile growth agency Moburst has built out a dedicated AI Engine Optimization practice aimed at established companies with existing app portfolios, betting that the category still lacks agencies with real depth rather than a rebranded service page. AI Engine Optimization, more commonly abbreviated AEO for Answer Engine Optimization, is the practice of structuring a brand’s content and web presence so AI systems such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google’s AI Overviews can confidently cite it when answering a user’s question directly, rather than showing a ranked list of links. For established companies vetting an AEO partner, the practical test is whether the agency can point to specific app-store-side work, not just web content changes, and whether it can describe a concrete process for reconciling inconsistent brand descriptions across many independent sources rather than treating that as someone else’s problem.

items.title: 1,100 AI workers sign letter asking US to support tools that 'pace the frontier of automated AI development' - Business Insider
items.summary: # Over 1,100 AI workers sign letter asking US to support tools that 'pace the frontier of automated AI development'. Senior officials at some of the nation's leading AI companies say it's time for the federal government to find a way to put the brakes on AI development if it's needed. "We request that the U.S. government support an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development," reads an open letter signed by more than 1,100 AI workers from companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta. The letter zeroes in on "automated AI development," which refers to when AI will be capable of developing itself, something the industry calls "Recursive Self-Improvement." Anthropic has shared that its Claude models are quickly approaching that threshold. Look out for an alert in your inbox the next time a new story is published!

items.summary: # HKT unveils self-developed AI platform HKT.AI One-stop hub for global AI resources, advancing "AI for All" in Hong Kong. HONG KONG SAR - Media OutReach Newswire - 28 July 2026 - HKT announces the launch of HKT.AI, a one-stop, integrated AI platform that enables businesses and individual customers to access a broad suite of prominent global AI resources through a single and intuitive interface. The platform aims to accelerate the mass adoption of AI in Hong Kong, especially in empowering SMEs in their digital transformation, and advance the vision of "AI for All.". HKT.AI aggregates a wide range of Chinese Mainland-based and global AI resources, enabling businesses and individuals to seamlessly access and switch across specialised applications and tools on a single platform to meet diverse work and everyday needs.

items.title: A 22-year-old makes $30,000 a month from children’s videos without ever showing his face or drawing a single frame.
items.summary:
A 22-year-old makes $30,000 a month from children’s videos without ever showing his face or drawing a single frame.

His younger brother watches the channel at breakfast without knowing who owns it.

One morning, the same episode played three times. The boy kept restarting it for the song and the familiar character. His brother sat across the table watching the exact replay loop that built the business.

He never begins with a blank page. He finds children’s videos that already earned millions of views and gives Claude the transcript and visual structure.

Claude extracts the mechanics without copying the story: song structure, character rhythm, scene pacing, opening hook and bright visual pattern. Then it writes an original episode around the same recurring hero used across his entire channel.

AI generates the voice and animation. He approves the episode and publishes it without drawing, filming or appearing on camera.

The $30,000 does not come from one viral cartoon. It comes from a growing library children recognize and replay while parents get a few quiet minutes.

His younger brother sees a cartoon.

YouTube sees repeat viewing.

He sees an asset that compounds every morning.

items.title: this creator just built a zero-delay auto-aim system on an $8 microcontroller
items.summary:
this creator just built a zero-delay auto-aim system on an $8 microcontroller

he deployed a custom local AI algorithm on a cheap ESP-32 to track human movement with absolute 0-pixel accuracy.

the system completely eliminates standard computation delay. it processes the bounding box and moves the sniper reticle instantly, locking onto the target in real time. the next step is hooking it up to a physical robotic arm.

it proves you don't need a massive GPU rig to run complex computer vision.

1. runs locally on a microcontroller
2. local AI inference for zero latency
3. 100% targeting precision

when an eight-dollar chip can track movement with zero latency, AI becomes dangerous local infrastructure. this article breaks down exactly how the ESP-32 is powering this physical hardware shift.

items.summary:

items.title: IoT & Industrial Robotics | Pipeline Magazine | IoT & Robotics
items.summary: Traditional industrial robots were designed around deterministic control systems. Tasks such as welding, assembly and material handling were optimized for consistency, with motion paths and parameters defined in advance. Any deviation from expected conditions required manual intervention, including reprogramming or recalibration. This approach constrained robotics to environments where variability could be minimized. [...] The integration of connected sensing and machine intelligence introduces closed-loop feedback mechanisms that fundamentally alter this model. Sensors embedded within equipment and the surrounding environment continuously capture variables such as force, vibration, temperature and spatial positioning. These data streams are analyzed in near real time, allowing robotic systems to adjust their actions dynamically. [...] This creates a shift in value from discrete components to pre-integrated connectivity platforms. A robotics OEM may not want to manage separate suppliers for radios, positioning, antennas, SIM/eSIM, security elements, certifications and network approvals. Instead, a pre-certified and lifecycle-managed connectivity subsystem can reduce integration burden, shorten deployment cycles and improve reliability in the field.

items.title: Developing Healthcare Robotics with GPU-Native Medical Physics Simulation
items.summary:
Healthcare robotics faces critical challenges in data scarcity, generalization, and development velocity due to limited access to annotated demonstrations, the prevalence of rare but clinically important scenarios, and slow, resource-intensive prototyping cycles. [...] AI-generated content may summarize information incompletely. Verify important information. Learn more

Unlike autonomous driving or industrial robotics, healthcare robotics can’t rely on internet-scale data collection or unlimited real-world experimentation. Every demonstration requires specialized equipment, clinical expertise, and access to patients or laboratory environments. This creates three fundamental challenges for developers. [...] The third challenge is development velocity. Medical robotics development relies on benchtop phantoms, cadaver studies, animal models, and limited clinical evaluations. These remain essential, but they are inherently sequential, expensive, and difficult to scale. Iterating on designs and algorithms currently takes months, pushing total development cycles to 4–7 years.

items.title: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to unde
items.summary: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.

items.title: How OpenAI Lost Control of an AI Model—and What ...
items.summary: OpenAI was evaluating its artificial intelligence models’ ability to exploit vulnerable software when instead the models hacked the infrastructure surrounding the test, broke containment, and attacked a real company, OpenAI revealed on July 21. Observers say this is the first real-world instance of AI doing something researchers have long worried about: a loss-of-control scenario. If the industry fails to learn from it, it is unlikely to be the last. [...] OpenAI did not respond to TIME’s request for comment, but has said it has partnered with Hugging Face to conduct a thorough investigation and will share more details once complete. But perhaps more worryingly, OpenAI is not legally compelled to disclose the incident in the first place.

items.title: How are companies, governments responding to the OpenAI hack?
items.summary:
ChatGPT owner OpenAI has admitted an “unprecedented cyber incident” – two of its most capable artificial intelligence models hacked into another AI company on their own – stirring debates over the need for stronger technology guardrails.

The company said its AI systems broke out of a testing environment and hacked startup Hugging Face.

The startup had disclosed on July 16 that its servers were hacked by an unknown but sophisticated agent acting on its own.
